answer.rationale: Write-path p99 started rising ~30m after the deploy, so the closest playbook is memory_b1 (rollback cleared a post-release checkout failure). That record was an error spike, not confirmed latency, so it is the one archive to re-read before committing. Circuit breaking is rejected: memory_b4 is fail-fast and would drop customer writes, which violates the objective. memory_b5 is report/read offload, not this write-heavy settlement path. memory_b3 is pre-peak headroom, not a demonstrated mid-peak write fix, and there is no regional signal for failover. Cause is still deploy vs saturation; one intervention window means the rollback must be large enough to restore availability but not an untested blast radius during settlement, hence standard_experiment, with downstream settlement-write risk flagged.
